The '''Supercopa de España''' ("Super Cup of Spain"), also referred as '''Spanish Super Cup''', is a [[super cup]] tournament in [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. Founded in [[1982 Supercopa de España|1982]] as a two-team competition, the current version has been contested since [[2020 Supercopa de España|2020]] by four teams: the winners and runners-up of the [[Copa del Rey]] and [[La Liga]].<ref name="rule">{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/sites/default/files/pdf/betting_in_english_0.pdf|title=Supercopa de España|website=www.rfef.es|access-date=13 January 2022|archive-date=13 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113124229/https://www.rfef.es/sites/default/files/pdf/betting_in_english_0.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

Until 1995, a team that won both the league and cup automatically got the trophy. From 1996 to 2019, if a team won both, they had to play the cup runners-up for the Supercopa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carratalá |first=José E. |date=2018-08-10 |title=Datos y récords de la Supercopa de España |url=https://elmagodelbalon.es/datos-y-records-de-la-supercopa-de-espana/ |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=El mago del balón |language=es |archive-date=19 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240319044106/https://elmagodelbalon.es/datos-y-records-de-la-supercopa-de-espana/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Cinco datos a saber de la Supercopa de España |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.es/es/noticias/3851789/cinco-datos-a-saber-de-la-supercopa-de-espana |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=www.fcbarcelona.es |language=es |archive-date=25 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725090603/https://www.fcbarcelona.es/es/noticias/3851789/cinco-datos-a-saber-de-la-supercopa-de-espana |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |date=2023-08-16 |title=Récords y estadísticas de la Supercopa de la UEFA |url=https://es.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c511879c5c3-fab847b383e3-1000--records-y-estadisticas-de-la-supercopa-de-la-uefa/ |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=[[UEFA]] |language=es |archive-date=19 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240319044105/https://es.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c511879c5c3-fab847b383e3-1000--records-y-estadisticas-de-la-supercopa-de-la-uefa/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Since its inception, thirteen teams have participated in the tournament, and ten have been crowned champions.

==History==
The current competition has existed since 1982. Between 1940 and 1953, several other tournaments between the Spanish league champions and the cup winners (then ''Copa del Generalísimo'') were played.<ref name=rsssf/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/detail/card/honours-football|title=Honours - FC Barcelona|website=FC Barcelona|access-date=16 August 2017|archive-date=23 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823051632/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/detail/card/honours-football|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=rfef15>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/noticias/rfef/historia-supercopa-precedentes-1936-1953|title=Historia de la Supercopa de España: ¿Sabías que durante unos años se llamó Copa Eva de Duarte y Perón?|trans-title=History of the Spanish Super Cup: Did you know that for a few years it was called the Eva de Duarte y Perón Cup?|language=es|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=3 August 2015|access-date=22 July 2020|archive-date=22 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200722164355/https://www.rfef.es/noticias/rfef/historia-supercopa-precedentes-1936-1953|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In September 1940, a match with this format had the name of [[Copa de los Campeones de España|Copa de Campeones]].<ref name=rfef15/> It was not repeated until December 1945 when, due to the good relations with the [[Francoist Spain|Spanish military government]] the [[ambassador]] of Argentina, offered a trophy called [[Copa de Oro Argentina]].<ref name=rsssf>[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spansupcuphist.html Spanish Supercup history] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521050006/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/spansupcuphist.html |date=21 May 2016 }}, [[RSSSF]]</ref><ref name=rfef15/> Both these trophies were unofficial and were only played once.<ref name=rsssf/>

In 1941, the [[1941–47 FEF President Cup|Copa Presidente FEF]] was established as an official tournament founded and organized by the RFEF; however, it was also only contested once, and though 11 of the 12 matches in its mini-league format were played between April and May 1941, its last, decisive fixture was delayed until eventually taking place in September 1947.<ref>[http://www.cihefe.es/cuadernosdefutbol/2018/04/el-torneo-mas-largo-de-la-historia-del-futbol-espanol-la-copa-del-presidente-de-la-rfef-1941-47/ El Torneo más largo de la historia del fútbol español. La Copa del presidente de la RFEF (1941-47) [The longest tournament in Spanish football history: The RFEF President's Cup (1941-47)&#93;], in Spanish, CIHEFE, 1 April 2018 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609054612/http://www.cihefe.es/cuadernosdefutbol/2018/04/el-torneo-mas-largo-de-la-historia-del-futbol-espanol-la-copa-del-presidente-de-la-rfef-1941-47/ |date=9 June 2023 }}</ref>

Also in 1947, the [[Copa Eva Duarte]] was established as an annual and official tournament founded and organized by the RFEF, as a tribute to Argentine president [[Juan Domingo Perón]] and his wife [[Eva Perón|María Eva Duarte de Perón]]. It was played between September and December, usually as one-match finals. The trophy was the predecessor of the current Supercopa de España, first held in 1982.<ref name=rsssf/><ref name=rfef15/>

In 2018, the Supercopa was played for the first time as a single match hosted at a neutral venue in [[Tangier]], [[Morocco]].<ref name=MARCA>{{cite web |url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/07/09/5b4354b122601de03a8b45e9.html |title=It's official: The Supercopa de Espana will be a one-legged match on August 12 |last=McTear |first=Euan |date=9 July 2018 |publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|MARCA]] |access-date=24 July 2018 |archive-date=15 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915224652/http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/07/09/5b4354b122601de03a8b45e9.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 12 November 2019, it was announced that the Supercopa would expand to four teams, the winners and runners-up of the [[Copa del Rey]] and [[La Liga]], and would be held at [[King Abdullah Sports City]] in [[Jeddah]], [[Saudi Arabia]] for the next three years, in a deal valued at €120 million. The event was also moved to January in order to reduce the "congestion" on teams' schedules.<ref name="rule"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2019/11/11/sports/soccer/11reuters-soccer-spain-supercup.html|title=Spanish Super Cup to Be Held in Saudi Arabia, Says Federation|date=11 November 2019|work=The New York Times|access-date=20 November 2019|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> The agreement has faced criticism: Jesus Álvarez, head of sport programming for state broadcaster [[RTVE]], stated that it would not bid for the media rights to the Supercopa, in protest of Saudi Arabia's [[Human rights in Saudi Arabia|human]] and [[Women's rights in Saudi Arabia|women's rights]] records—especially [[Women's sport in Saudi Arabia|in women's sports]]. [[Liga de Fútbol Profesional|Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional]] president [[Javier Tebas]] also criticized the decision, citing the human rights violations and the country's "pirating" of European football (in reference to pirate broadcaster [[beoutQ]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportbusiness.com/news/tebas-criticises-spanish-super-cup-saudi-plans-given-piracy-association/|title=Tebas criticises Spanish Super Cup Saudi plans given piracy association|date=14 November 2019|website=SportBusiness|language=en-US|access-date=20 November 2019|archive-date=4 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704172543/https://www.sportbusiness.com/news/tebas-criticises-spanish-super-cup-saudi-plans-given-piracy-association/|url-status=live}}</ref> In the past, Tebas had been a major advocate to hold the competition outside of Spain, and especially in the [[United States]], as part of his efforts to expand La Liga globally.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Panja|first=Tariq|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/20/sports/soccer/spain-soccer-saudi-arabia.html|title=La Liga Chief Claims Saudi Arabia Is Using Sports to 'Whitewash' Reputation|date=20 January 2020|work=The New York Times|access-date=28 February 2020|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=19 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819003746/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/01/20/sports/soccer/spain-soccer-saudi-arabia.html|url-status=live}}</ref> RFEF president [[Luis Rubiales]] stated that women would be able to attend the matches without restriction, and defended the agreement as the use of football to "transform society".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/spanish-super-cup-saudi-arabia-rfef-adidas/|title=Spanish Super Cup to be held in Saudi Arabia for three years|website=SportsPro|date=12 November 2019|access-date=20 November 2019|archive-date=13 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113200352/https://www.sportspromedia.com/news/spanish-super-cup-saudi-arabia-rfef-adidas/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50380282|title=Spanish Super Cup: Saudi Arabia to host Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid and Valencia|work=BBC Sport|date=11 November 2019|access-date=20 November 2019|archive-date=4 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704172541/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50380282|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportspro.com/news/rtve-spanish-super-cup-saudi-arabia-human-rights-concerns/|title=RTVE won't bid for Spanish Super Cup amid Saudi human rights concerns|website=SportsPro|date=15 November 2019|access-date=20 November 2019|archive-date=8 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210308102253/https://www.sportspromedia.com/news/rtve-spanish-super-cup-saudi-arabia-human-rights-concerns|url-status=live}}</ref>

In one semi-final, the La Liga champion plays the Copa del Rey runner-up, while in the other the Copa del Rey winner plays the La Liga runner-up. Neither the Copa del Rey nor La Liga winners reached the Supercopa de España final in the first three editions of the four-team format,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/supercopa-of-spain/madrid-vs-athletic-there-will-be-champion-of-the-supercopa-2022-without-national-titles_276907_102.html|title=Madrid vs Athletic: There will be a champion of the 2022 Super Cup without national titles|website=FC Barcelona Noticias|date=14 January 2022|access-date=17 January 2022|archive-date=4 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704172546/https://www.fcbarcelonanoticias.com/en/supercopa-of-spain/madrid-vs-athletic-there-will-be-champion-of-the-supercopa-2022-without-national-titles_276907_102.html|url-status=live}}</ref> while Barcelona played Real Madrid in each final of the next four editions. In June 2021, the extension of the agreement with Saudi Arabia for ten years was announced, to continue playing the tournament in the country until at least 2029.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-07 |title=Arabia Saudí acogerá la Supercopa de España hasta 2029 |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/supercopa-espana/2021/06/07/60bdcf39ca47419b288b4580.html |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=MARCA |language=es |archive-date=4 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240104034706/https://www.marca.com/futbol/supercopa-espana/2021/06/07/60bdcf39ca47419b288b4580.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-07 |title=La Supercopa de España se jugará en Arabia Saudí hasta 2029 |url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20210607/supercopa-espana-jugara-arabia-saudi/587191718_0.html |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=El Español |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-14 |title=¿Por qué la Supercopa de España se disputa en Arabia Saudí? |url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/supercopa/supercopa-espana-disputa-arabia-saudi-96311248 |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=www.sport.es |language=es |archive-date=19 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240319045607/https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/supercopa/supercopa-espana-disputa-arabia-saudi-96311248 |url-status=live }}</ref> Due to a conflict with the [[2027 AFC Asian Cup]], which Saudi Arabia will host, the 2027 Supercopa would be moved to [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Díaz |first1=José Félix |title=Estambul, sede de la Supercopa de España |url=https://as.com/futbol/estambul-sede-de-la-supercopa-de-espana-f202608-n/ |access-date=13 August 2026 |work=Diario AS |date=13 August 2026 |language=es}}</ref>
